en: Theragāthā 5.10 Pañcaka-nipāta First Chapter (Paṭhama-vagga)
The Verses of Yasadatta Thera:
“One of a malicious mind and dull-witted hears the teaching of the Conqueror;”
The fool, with a mind intent on finding fault, stands far from the true Dhamma, just as the earth is distant from the sky.
One hears the teaching of the Conqueror,
yet falls away from the true Dhamma like the moon in the dark fortnight.
The foolish person, with a mind intent on finding fault,
hears the teaching of the Conqueror;
he withers away in the True Dhamma.
Just as a fish in the water,
the foolish one with a mind intent on fault-finding hears the teaching of the Conqueror.
He does not grow in the True Dharma,
like a rotten seed in a field; but he who,
with a contented mind, [proceeds]...
He hears the teaching of the Conqueror;
having exhausted all taints,
he has realized the unshakable state.
“Having attained supreme peace,
the one whose taints have been extinguished enters final Nibbāna.
… Thus spoke the elder Yasadatta.
